ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Act); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 implementing the RBE Act; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 20-744 on AML/CFT obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry or consular authority of the holder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille unless expressly waived under the Luxembourg RBE Act for registered EU/EEA documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of residence / proof of current residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local electricity, water, or banking institution in the owner's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / excerpt of commercial register for any corporate shareholder or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming primary payment rails (Stripe/PayPal settlement account) and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the e-commerce settlement account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the incorporator or authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the representative's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Luxembourg national list of politically exposed persons, EU Council sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and, for international best practice, the U.S. OFAC SDN list; enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval required for any PEP, negative media, or sanctions hit; continuous screening prior to incorporation and quarterly after establishment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in Luxembourgish, French, German, or English, but must be written in Latin characters; for SCSp the name must contain the words 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'; French or German legal forms must be transliterated consistently across all official filings; non-Latin characters are not accepted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written request with the Registration Department of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of notification, providing evidence of distinctive character and non-confusion with existing marks; if the administrative appeal fails, a formal application may be made to the Luxembourg administrative court (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the definitive refusal, with right to seek interim suspension under Articles 39 and 40 of the Administrative Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual or domiciliation office is permissible for an SCSp exclusively engaged in online sales of maternity and infant care commodities, provided the registered office is physically located in Luxembourg at the premises of a CSSF-approved domiciliation agent or law firm; the substantive management activities, administrative accounting, and UBO register files may be maintained by the domiciliation agent, although the anti-abuse substance doctrine requires an adequate track record of local decision-making if tax treaty benefits are to be claimed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Moderate (estimated annual probability of 12% for domiciliation-office SCSp entities; RCS, tax authorities, and CSSF may conduct unannounced inspections during the first three years, particularly where the entity claims treaty protection or applies for a VAT registration number).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff (€14–€75) plus professional service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
Publication of the formation documents in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)

AML/KYC due diligence file, PEP and sanctions screening, UBO structure analysis and qualification memos

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 (SCSp regime), specifically Articles 102-139 and Article 102-1; related provisions of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on the Annual Accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 12, avenue de la Gare, L-1611 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (statuts) executed as a private deed or notarial deed, together with RCS incorporation form (Form B) and the declaration of beneficial owner; filed via the LBR e-incorporation portal or in person at the RCS registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); capital is freely determined by the partnership agreement. No escrow or bank blockage rule applies to cash contributions under Luxembourg law, provided each contribution is fully paid up at the time contributions are recorded and listed in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolution of the General Partner of [SCSp name], adopted on [date]. The General Partner resolves: (1) to approve the initial capital contributions of the Limited Partners and confirm the capital table; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) to appoint Mr./Ms. [name] as Gérant with sole and exclusive authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the partnership; (4) to authorise the Gérant to file the incorporation deed with the RCS and to complete all registration formalities; (5) on Vesting. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online name search portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the RCS database to confirm the proposed partnership name is available and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Submit a formal name reservation request through the LBR e-incorporation platform, specifying the SCSp legal form. There is no mandatory prior name clearance for ordinary trading names that do not contain regulated words; if the intended name includes terminology such as 'fund', 'bank', or 'insurance', a separate letter of non-objection from the CSSF or Ministry of the Economy may be required.
required_dossiers: Proposed name reservation form (Form A)
Identification documents of the general partner and authorized representative
Power of attorney to Luxembourg counsel (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags a conflicting name or a similarity dispute, file a new reservation request with an alternative denomination. The applicant may appeal the Registrar's rejection to the District Court of Luxembourg within 15 days of notification under Articles 23-24 of the Law of 19 December 2002.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public for notarial execution; alternatively the SCSp general partner where a private deed (sous seing privé) is permitted, provided no in-kind contributions or real estate transfers are involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, German, or English (English permitted for SCSp). The deed must include: the legal form (SCSp), corporate name, registered office municipality in Luxembourg, duration (unlimited or fixed), object clause covering online retail of maternity and infant care commodities (ISIC 4791), contribution amounts and payment schedule, identity of the general partner (gerant) and limited partners, and the general partner's unlimited liability provision. Execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary or by private act; ensure the contribution schedule is signed and each partner's identity is verified under AML/KYC requirements of the Law of 12 November 2004.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Passport copies of all general and limited partners
Proof of residential or business address of partners (utility bill or bank statement)
Bank confirmation of capital contribution for cash-funded subscription (if required)
Tax compliance certificates (certificat de non-collecte) for foreign partners, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a partner identifies a defect or missing information, issue a corrective pleading and re-execute the deed in a supplementary act (acte rectificatif). Where the RCS later queries the deed, a conforming amendment resolution must be adopted and filed within the statutory cure period of one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation File with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg – filing via LBR e-incorporation portal (https://e-incorporation.lbr.lu) or in-person counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed Articles of Association, the RCS Form A (appointment of legal representative/receiver), Form B (entity data), and the declaration of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration). The RCS will verify the deed against statutory requirements, confirm payment of the registration fee, and issue the RCS registration number and certificate of incorporation. For an SCSp with no majority control by a Luxembourg resident, the RCS will also register the foreign general partner and may request additional proof of identity and authority.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Articles of Association
RCS Form A (legal representative powers)
RCS Form B (entity information)
Beneficial owner declaration (Article 3 of the Law of 13 January 2019)
Office lease or registered office acceptance letter in Luxembourg
Proof of payment of the official filing fee (EUR 75 dossier fee plus EUR 75 publication fee approx.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RCS issues a query letter (lettre de rejet) citing deficiencies. Respond with a corrective filing, amending deed, or supplementary declaration within one month; an appeal against refusal is available to the District Court under the Law of 19 December 2002. Late filing after business commencement exposes the gérant to daily fines under Article 21 of the same law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), published by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice / LBR platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the Registrar automatically transmits the deed and the statutory notices to RESA. Verify that the published data correctly reflects the name, registered office, object, capital, and legal representatives. Pay the governmental publication fee (included in the initial official filing fee). Monitor publication to ensure the SCSp is effective against third parties as of the date of publication in RESA.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Original executed Articles of Association (for publication annex)
Receipt of official filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA rejects or suspends publication due to incomplete metadata, submit a corrected notice within 15 business days. Where acts are not published within the legal deadline, the SCSp may invoke non-opposability to third parties; curative re-publication resolves this once the full text is published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registry, VAT, and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (ADA), as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the national business number (numéro d'identification national) generated by the LBR and linked to the RCS. Register for VAT (TVA) with the AEDT within 15 days of commencing economic activity, using the standard VAT registration form (Formulaire TVA 1) or via the MyGuichet.lu portal. Since the entity will engage in e-commerce of baby and maternity supplies to consumers, apply for a Luxembourg VAT number and, where distance sales thresholds are exceeded, register in other EU member states under the OSS system. If employees are hired, register as an employer with the CCSS to obtain an employer registration number and enrol in social security schemes. Optionally apply for an EORI number if goods are imported from third countries.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and certificate of incorporation
Articles of Association (certified copy)
Gérant identity document and proof of address
Description of business activity (ISIC 4791 online retail)
Bank account details of the SCSp
Information on expected turnover for VAT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration triggers a penalty of EUR 50 to EUR 500 under Article 21 of the VAT law. If the AEDT rejects the registration or requests clarifications regarding the place of supply for e-commerce, file an administrative appeal within three months and submit corrected turnover projections or a formal written explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale de l'Industrie et du Commerce (General Directorate for Industry and Commerce), 19-21 boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license is required for online retail of maternity and infant care commodities (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 458110) under Luxembourg law. If the SCSp operates a physical stock warehouse in Luxembourg, a Classified Establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement classé) may apply under the Law of 10 June 1999 on Classified Establishments. A retail sales permit (commercial licence) is not required for pure e-commerce operators without a physical point of sale.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Environmental Permitting Division.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 4: non-industrial e-commerce warehousing and logistics operations below the statutory thresholds of Annex 1 to the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 1999 on Classified Establishments; no mandatory full EIA report or environmental impact assessment registration is required for this business scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to public sewers must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2013 implementing the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (91/271/EEC); volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from any packaging or printing operations must respect the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 11 January 2008 (transposing Directive 2004/42/EC); packaging waste must be managed through the national VALORLUX take-back scheme with an annual packaging waste declaration; ozone-depleting substances and fluorinated greenhouse gases from warehouse cooling equipment must follow Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 and Luxembourg implementing rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification requires an inspection and approval letter from the Administration des Services de Secours (Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps) for any warehouse or storage area exceeding 1,000 m² or holding substantial combustible materials. A structural load clearance certificate from the municipal building authority (certificat de charge structurale) is required for warehouse racking and mezzanine floors. Occupational health and workplace safety clearance is issued by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering emergency exit plans, fire extinguisher compliance, electrical installation checks, and mandatory workplace risk assessments under the Labour Code (Articles L.311-1 et seq.).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs) for export controls. Unified business e-administration portal: MyGuichet.lu; VAT e-filing: eTVA portal; company registry: RCSL e-Registre.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SCSp and file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) to obtain the matricule and national business number. Step 2 - File Form 640 for VAT identification with the AEDT Bureau d'identification TVA via MyGuichet.lu; a non-established foreign partner supplying through the SCSp must register in its own name and, if a non-EU resident, appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (Article 61 VAT Law). Step 3 - Obtain the Luxembourg VAT number in the format 'LU + 8 digits + check digit'. Step 4 - Obtain an EORI number from Luxembourg Customs before any export declaration. Step 5 - Register for the Union OSS / IOSS schemes on the Luxembourg portal if the SCSp makes EU consumer distance sales. Step 6 - Foreign founders without Luxembourg residence must appoint a local tax representative for direct tax notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp has no legal personality and is fiscally transparent by law: it is not subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICB) or net wealth tax (IFI). Income, gains, and net assets are attributed directly to partners under the partnership agreement and taxed at partner level (corporate partner: up to 24.94% combined in Luxembourg City; individual partner: progressive personal income tax). For VAT, the SCSp is similarly transparent and supplies are deemed made by the partners unless the SCSp has an independent fixed establishment and is separately registered as a taxable person. Territorial scope: unitary national, no sub-national VAT or sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification exists; SCSp transparency is mandatory. Available elections: (i) voluntary VAT registration waiving the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); (ii) election to form a VAT group ('assujetti unique') with Luxembourg-established related persons (Article 60 VAT Law); (iii) election of the OSS/IOSS one-stop-shop schemes for cross-border consumer sales; (iv) ATAD hybrid-mismatch grandfathering election for pre-2019 hybrid instruments (Law of 21 December 2018; hybrid mismatch reporting form 708); (v) election to register as a regulated SIF/SICAR fund (CSSF authorization) with separate tax regimes. No election can render the SCSp opaque for corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) implemented under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC; not a GST or sales-and-use tax. Luxembourg rate bands: 3% super-reduced (foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals, baby formula if classified as food), 8% reduced (certain essential consumer goods; per-product classification for maternity/baby items required), 14% intermediate, 17% standard. Excise duties do not attach to ISIC 4791 e-commerce goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-enterprise exemption (Article 57 VAT Law). Below this threshold registration remains voluntary; mandatory registration applies from the first euro for EU distance sales when OSS/IOSS is elected, for intra-EU acquisitions above the EUR 10,000 distance-sales threshold, and for non-established suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or invoice-authorization regime. Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing to Luxembourg public entities via PEPPOL (PEPPOL BIS 3.0). VAT returns and OSS/IOSS statements are filed electronically via eTVA and MyGuichet.lu. No continuous transaction-level API clearance, no SAF-T, and no QR/fiscal-code invoice clearance applies to e-commerce merchants; paper, PDF, and structured e-invoices are equally acceptable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Maternity and baby goods physically dispatched from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% export exemption (Article 40 VAT Law) on proof of departure from the EU obtained within 90 days of supply (Article 74 VAT Law). Intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered traders are exempt under Article 43 with a valid EU VAT number and EC Sales List. Distance sales to EU consumers are not zero-rated: they are taxable at destination via Union OSS (goods above EUR 150) or IOSS (goods not above EUR 150). The SCSp must retain PSP settlement records (Stripe/PayPal) as payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) with exit confirmation from Luxembourg Customs and the Export Accompanying Document (EAD)
Bill of Lading (or alternative transport document: air waybill / CMR) evidencing dispatch from Luxembourg to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate: bank credit advice or PSP settlement report (Stripe/PayPal merchant statement) matching the export invoice
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the maternity/baby goods and their value
EORI number of the exporting SCSp and, where applicable, customs representation / power of attorney letter
VAT registration proof and, for intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT number with EC Sales List reference
Proof of export timing (entry into transport registry or customs log within 90 days of the supply)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT cross-checks eTVA returns, OSS statements, and customs exit data. If proof of export is not produced within 90 days, or the goods did not leave the EU, the 0% rate is clawed back and Luxembourg VAT up to 17% is assessed with late-payment interest (0.6% per month, Article 31 VAT Law). Administrative fines range up to 100% of evaded tax (Article 65 VAT Law); obstruction penalties follow Article 66; criminal tax fraud under Sections 396-398 of the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) carries imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000. The 'abus de droit' doctrine permits recharacterization of artificial export routing. SCSp partners may be held jointly and severally liable for clawback, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking prudential supervision and foreign exchange reporting compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc has been replaced by the euro; the euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg operates an open market economy with no exchange controls on either the current or capital account. Repatriation of profits, dividends, and redemption proceeds from a SCSp is not subject to Luxembourg exchange control approval. The principal regulatory hurdles are documentary: adequate proof of underlying economic activity, compliance with EU anti-money laundering directives, and statistical reporting of cross-border payments under BCL regulations. For tax-transparent SCSp, profit remittance to foreign partners is not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, however domestic tax law may require proof of the partnership's tax-transparent classification to avoid significant deemed withholding or administrative scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists in Luxembourg for the surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds into EUR. The euro is the sole legal tender and the free movement of capital is enshrined in EU law. Export receipts may be retained in any currency of the exporter's choice, subject only to standard banking due diligence and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds. The mandatory conversion ratio is therefore 0%, and no timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) without a Luxembourg passport or physical branch face significant legal constraints in providing main transaction accounts to a Luxembourg SCSp. Under PSD2, an EMI must be authorized or passported through the CSSF; cross-border remote onboarding is generally permitted only after CSSF notification and compliance with Luxembourg KYC/AML obligations. For a non-resident managed SCSp operating cross-border e-commerce, a CSSF-authorized EMI or an EU-passported EMI with Luxembourg market notification is usable for operational liquidity, but high-volume clearing, multi-currency needs, and merchant settlement resilience are better supported by a tier-1 bank. Regtech-forward EMIs that partner with a Luxembourg credit institution remain viable for payment acceptance and disbursement flow, subject to the SCSp's ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and source-of-funds documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence for directors is generally required for the final account mandate, but most Luxembourg banks permit a remote video-interview and e-signature channel for low-risk corporate clients, provided the SCSp's appointed Luxembourg domiciliation agent and registered office are verified. The natural-person director or designated authorized signatory must undergo a live video KYC call; physical attendance at a bank branch is typically waived for clients in regulated industries with reliable UBO identification. For high-risk client categories, including complex ownership structures or non-EU resident partners, banks retain the discretionary right to request a physical meeting in Luxembourg or at the bank's Paris/Brussels/Frankfurt hub.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex and non-transparent ownership structure of the SCSp (absence of a fund-licensed manager or non-EU limited partners with opaque holdings)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the constitutive deed of the SCSp, the partner register with full UBO names, birth dates, nationalities, and addresses, notarized signatures, up-to-date excerpt from the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS), and a written explanation of each partner's source of wealth and source of funds, supported by audited financial statements where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-EU jurisdiction without clear underlying trade purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a fully documented capital subscription agreement, board or partner resolutions, bank references from the remitting institution, and an opening balance-sheet projection evidencing the commercial purpose of the e-commerce business. Include a structured schedule of incoming wire transfers and relevant customs/import-export documentation for baby and maternity supplies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high transaction velocity relative to initial capital size for an online retail entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide historical e-commerce merchant analytics, supply agreements with manufacturers, logistics and fulfillment contracts, platform payout reports (e.g. Stripe, PayPal), and a detailed treasury forecast demonstrating that the activity is ordinary course and not structured to avoid AML thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or boycott alignment of partners, customers, or suppliers routed through a high-risk corridor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Run and submit a sanctions screening result for all UBOs, directors, and transaction counterparties using an independent screening tool; provide publicly available ownership and control-chain charts; and execute contractual sanctions-relevant representations and warranties in favour of the Luxembourg bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's or parent's bank to the SCSp operational account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire must state a clear and accurate purpose code, typically 'BOP_G_OTHER_INVESTMENT' or 'S12' depending on the BCL reporting manual, and clearly identify the sender and beneficiary with the SCSp's IBAN. Verification requires the bank to obtain the underlying capital contribution deed, proof of the initiating party's identity, and evidence that the injection does not violate any EU sanctions or counter-terrorism financing rules. Payment messages should explicitly use 'BEN' or 'OUR' reimbursement per bilateral bank instructions and include an awareness statement if the value exceeds EUR 10,000 equivalent for automatic Currency Transaction Reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for high-value supplier payments and for final settlements under documentary credits. For confirmed purchase transactions in baby and maternity supplies, a confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg SCSp's bank in favour of the overseas supplier is recommended, with Incoterms, inspection certificates, and transport documents attached. The SCSp must ensure that the LC is compliant with UCP 600, contains a precise Goods Description matching ISIC 4791, and is covered by the bank's funds release criteria. Payments to freight forwarders, consolidators, and customs brokers should be executed via SEPA Wire, MT103, or cross-border ACH where the counterparty is in the EU, while non-EU suppliers require correspondent banking rails via SWIFT. All outbound payments must be accompanied by the underlying invoice, purchase order, and proof of logistics movement to satisfy the bank's AML/CTF narrative requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency Forward (FX Forward) — spot/forward deal with a Luxembourg-authorized bank or broker to lock in EUR/USD and EUR/CNY conversion rates for known trade flows

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) — permitted for hedging exposures in currencies with limited convertibility or where local settlement is prohibited, provided the counterparty is an EU-licensed credit institution
Cross-Currency Swap — permitted for medium-term asset/liability matching where the SCSp holds foreign currency revenue while paying EUR-denominated costs
Plain Vanilla Currency Option — permitted for protective hedging against adverse FX moves in high-volume e-commerce settlement currencies, executed through licensed EU investment firms

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner accuracy confirmation (RBE annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 30 June; beneficial-owner changes must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 50,000 for incorrect or incomplete filing; intentional concealment is a criminal offence carrying up to 5 years' imprisonment and/or criminal fines up to EUR 500,000; no direct administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and management report (publication obligation if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking or a regulated alternative investment fund)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fines up to EUR 1,000 per day after formal notice; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger RCS administrative strike-off proceedings and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership tax information return (form 563 / taxable-results declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually; for a calendar-year SCSp, no later than 31 December of the following year for e-filers, with earlier paper-filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and default assessments under Luxembourg General Tax Law, typically a surcharge up to 10% of the tax due and daily fines of EUR 10–25; repeated non-compliance may result in criminal fines for the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is triggered when the undertaking exceeds two of the three following thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average full-time staff 50. A SCSp must also be audited if it is a regulated alternative investment fund/RAIF, or where the partnership agreement requires audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended); IFRS may be applied for consolidated or voluntary accounts; tax-transparent results are computed in accordance with the Luxembourg Income Tax Act (LIR).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner maintains the SCSp's partner register and UBO records. A transfer of a limited-partner interest is effective once notified to the general partner and reflected in the register; if the transfer causes a beneficial owner to cross the 25% ownership or control threshold, the RBE must be updated within 30 days. The accuracy of the RBE filing must be confirmed online at least once every calendar year before 30 June.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners
